public_rationale: OpenAI's February 27, 2025 announcement described GPT-4.5 as more expensive than GPT-4o [e2]. On April 14, 2025, OpenAI announced GPT-4.1 and reported that it was 26% less expensive than GPT-4o for median queries [e1]. That newer model's lower published API pricing provides a counterexample to the claim that OpenAI's latest models only get more expensive [e1].
limitations: These disclosures concern customer API prices; they do not establish OpenAI's internal inference spending [e1, e2].
The 26% comparison applies to median queries and does not establish savings for every workload or per completed task [e1].
GPT-4.5's higher price supports the narrower observation that an individual release could be more expensive [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's latest models keep getting more expensive over time.

statement.excerpt: DeepSeek is not OpenAI, and OpenAI’s latest models only get more expensive as time drags on.

from_speaker: OpenAI’s latest models only get more expensive as time drags on
GPT-4.5 costs $75 per million input tokens, and $150 per million output tokens
our_interpretation: The adjacent per-token figures identify customer API prices as the ordinary measure of expensive.
Assess the recent model releases in 2025 through the post date. This is an observation about the release trend, not an indefinite forecast.
Only makes the statement stronger than saying that some models are expensive. A comparable newer model offered at lower prices is a counterexample.
A cheaper model's release need not establish that every model or every workload becomes cheaper.
criteria.support_condition: Published API prices show that successive comparable recent OpenAI models consistently became more expensive.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Before the post, OpenAI released a comparable newer model at lower API prices than its predecessor or the existing model it was replacing.
